stories.title: Bitcoin options price a quiet CPI week, with shorts clustered at $76,000–$80,000
stories.summary: Options market data shows traders positioning for a calm week around the upcoming CPI release, with bearish bets concentrated in the $76,000–$80,000 range. The pricing suggests the market does not expect a large swing in either direction from the inflation report.
stories.whyItMatters: Options positioning gives a read on where professional traders see risk, a useful gauge separate from spot price noise.
whatToWatch: The CPI release and Bitcoin's reaction
Whether the $76,000–$80,000 short cluster holds or gets squeezed
questions: Will actual CPI data match the low-volatility expectation priced into options?

stories.title: Thailand seeks a role in the $120 billion Bitcoin and Ethereum ETF market, on its own terms
stories.summary: Thailand is moving to join the global Bitcoin and Ethereum ETF market, which CryptoSlate puts at roughly $120 billion, but wants its own regulatory framework rather than copying other jurisdictions. Details on the proposed structure were not specified in the available reporting.
stories.whyItMatters: A new national entrant into crypto ETFs would expand regulated access to digital assets in Southeast Asia and could influence how other regional regulators approach approval.
whatToWatch: Formal rules or filings from Thai regulators
Which local institutions seek to launch products first
questions: What specific terms would differ from US or Hong Kong ETF frameworks?

sources.title: Thailand wants a piece of the $120 billion Bitcoin and Ethereum ETF market, but on its own terms

stories.title: FTX's former Bitcoin mining bet gets new life as parent raises €800 million for AI
stories.summary: A Bitcoin mining operation once tied to FTX has found new purpose, as its parent company raised €800 million to fund AI infrastructure. The report frames this as mining infrastructure being repurposed toward the AI buildout rather than staying focused on Bitcoin mining alone.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows how crypto-mining infrastructure and capital are being redirected toward AI compute demand, a trend reshaping miner business models industry-wide.
whatToWatch: How the €800 million is deployed between AI and mining operations
Whether other former FTX-linked assets see similar pivots
questions: How much of the original Bitcoin mining capacity remains active versus converted to AI use?

sources.title: FTX’s former Bitcoin mining bet gets new life as parent raises €800 million for AI

stories.title: Bitcoin's rebound approaches $85,000, a zone where past buyers may sell
stories.summary: Bitcoin's price has been recovering and is nearing the $85,000 level, an area on-chain data suggests holds a concentration of prior buyers who could sell to break even or lock in gains. That kind of supply overhead can slow or stall a rally as it approaches.
stories.whyItMatters: Price levels tied to past buyer cost basis often act as resistance, making this a key level for traders watching whether the rebound continues.
whatToWatch: Whether Bitcoin tests and holds above $85,000
Volume and selling pressure as the price nears that zone
questions: How much supply is actually held near this cost basis versus already moved?

sources.title: Bitcoin’s rebound approaches the $85,000 zone where past buyers may sell

stories.title: Solana proposal would let offline-signed approvals stay valid after a failed transaction
stories.summary: A new proposal for Solana addresses a quirk in offline transaction signing, where an approval can remain valid even after the transaction it was meant for fails. The change aims to close a gap that could let a stale signed approval be reused unexpectedly.
stories.whyItMatters: Signing and approval bugs are a common source of wallet exploits, so fixing this closes a potential security gap for Solana users.
whatToWatch: Whether the proposal is adopted by Solana's core development process
Wallet and app updates implementing the fix
questions: Has this issue been exploited already, or was it caught before misuse?

sources.title: Solana’s offline-signing proposal would keep approvals valid after failed transactions

stories.title: Global watchdog warns $300 billion stablecoin market could still face bank-run risk
stories.summary: An international financial watchdog has warned that the roughly $300 billion stablecoin market remains vulnerable to bank-run-style dynamics, even when issuers hold full reserves. The concern centers on how quickly holders could demand redemptions faster than reserves can be liquidated.
stories.whyItMatters: Stablecoins underpin much of crypto trading and settlement, so a credible run-risk warning from a global regulator could shape upcoming reserve and liquidity rules.
whatToWatch: Specific policy recommendations following the warning
Reactions from major stablecoin issuers
questions: Which watchdog issued the warning, and does it have authority to set binding rules?

sources.title: Global watchdog warns the $300 billion stablecoin market could face bank runs even with full reserves

stories.title: France's tax proposal would tax Bitcoin-to-USDC swaps before investors cash out
stories.summary: A French tax proposal would apply tax at the point of swapping Bitcoin for USDC, rather than waiting until an investor converts back to euros or another fiat currency. This would treat crypto-to-crypto swaps as taxable events.
stories.whyItMatters: Taxing swaps between crypto assets, not just cash-outs, would be a stricter standard than many jurisdictions use and could affect how investors structure trades in France.
whatToWatch: Whether the proposal advances through the French legislature
Reaction from crypto exchanges operating in France
questions: Would the rule apply retroactively or only to future swaps?

sources.title: France’s tax proposal would tax Bitcoin-to-USDC swaps before investors cash out

stories.title: Standard Chartered brings Ripple's RLUSD into banking custody after $765 million quarterly surge
stories.summary: Standard Chartered is now providing custody for Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin, following a quarter in which the token's supply or volume reportedly grew by $765 million. The move brings a major global bank directly into the custody chain for a stablecoin.
stories.whyItMatters: A large bank taking on custody signals growing institutional comfort with stablecoins and could boost confidence in RLUSD specifically.
whatToWatch: RLUSD adoption and supply growth in coming quarters
Other banks following with similar custody arrangements
questions: What specifically drove the $765 million quarterly increase?

sources.title: Standard Chartered brings Ripple’s RLUSD into banking custody after $765 million quarterly surge

stories.title: Eclair merges fixes for Lightning Network flaws that could burn Bitcoin in fees
stories.summary: The Eclair Lightning Network implementation has merged fixes for flaws that could have caused users to lose Bitcoin to excessive fees. The specific attack or bug mechanics were not detailed beyond the fee-loss risk.
stories.whyItMatters: Lightning is a key Bitcoin scaling layer, so fee-related bugs in major implementations like Eclair directly affect the cost and safety of everyday Lightning payments.
whatToWatch: Rollout of the fix across Eclair node operators
Whether other Lightning implementations carry the same flaw
questions: Were any funds actually lost before the fix was merged?

sources.title: Eclair merges fixes for Lightning flaws that could burn Bitcoin in fees

stories.title: EU targets MiCA loophole letting one license cover crypto exchanges in all 27 countries
stories.summary: EU regulators are moving to close a gap in the MiCA framework that currently lets a crypto exchange serve all 27 member states on the strength of a single national license. The effort suggests concern that some licenses are being used as an easy entry point to the whole bloc.
stories.whyItMatters: MiCA is the EU's flagship crypto regulation, so changes to its licensing rules would directly affect how exchanges operate and expand across Europe.
whatToWatch: Formal rule changes or guidance from EU regulators
Which licensing jurisdictions face the most scrutiny
questions: Which specific national licenses are seen as the easiest route into the loophole?

sources.title: EU targets MiCA loophole that lets crypto exchanges serve 27 countries with one license
